A packet a process generates inside the namespace never crosses prerouting: it goes out through output and postrouting. Without an output trace chain, none of the rules it meets ever appears in the trace.

docs.title: Turning it on
docs.text:
from nse.core.rule_engine import RuleEngine

RuleEngine(trace_output=True).load(rules, ns.name)

This adds a chain nse_trace_output to NSE's nse_trace table, in the output hook at priority -350. That is ahead of raw (-300), mangle (-150), DNAT (-100) and filter (0), so the trace flag is set before any of your chains sees the packet. By default it is off, and the trace is exactly what it was before.

docs.title: Proving the monitor is attached
docs.text:
TraceHarvester.wait_ready() proves only that this process is reading the monitor's output, not that nft monitor trace has subscribed to the kernel. A trace that is not attached is empty, and an empty trace reads as "no rule matched".

stimuli.trace_ready() closes that. It sends a canary stimulus from the sandbox until the canary's own trace comes back, up to attempts times. Only an event for the canary's destination, transport and port counts, so background traffic does not count as proof:

import asyncio

from nse import ProcessIdentity, stimuli
from nse.core.rule_engine import RuleEngine
from nse.core.trace_harvester import TraceHarvester

DROP_NOBODY = """
table inet egress {
    chain out {
        type filter hook output priority 0; policy accept;
        meta skuid 65534 udp dport 9999 drop
    }
}
"""

async def test_the_drop_rule_is_what_stops_nobody() -> None:
    RuleEngine(trace_output=True).load(DROP_NOBODY, ns.name)
    harvester = TraceHarvester()
    events = []
    await harvester.start(ns.name, asyncio.Queue(), timeout=20.0, on_event=events.append)
    try:
        await harvester.wait_ready()
        readiness = await stimuli.trace_ready(
            harvester, ns, stimuli.udp("10.0.1.1", 7777),
            identity=ProcessIdentity(uid=1000, gid=1000),
        )
        assert readiness.ready, readiness.describe()

        await stimuli.udp("10.0.1.1", 9999).run(ns, identity=ProcessIdentity(uid=65534, gid=65534))
        await asyncio.sleep(0.5)
    finally:
        state = await harvester.aclose()

    subject = readiness.without(events)  # the canary's traces removed
    assert [e for e in subject if e.type == "match" and "drop" in (e.rule_text or "")]

readiness.without(events) drops every trace that touched the canary, including traces whose lines arrived after readiness was decided. Give the canary a destination that nothing else in the test uses.

An attempt that could_not_run is not a canary: it is listed in readiness.problems, and it never counts as proof. If the monitor died, its health errors are listed too.

For a lower-level canary, call harvester.prove_ready(send, predicate) with your own send coroutine. It returns None, or the reason it could not send.

docs.title: The blind case
docs.text: Without trace_output=True, a canary sent from inside the sandbox is never traced. trace_ready() then returns ready=False rather than an empty trace that looks like a pass. NSE's own tests run both cases.

docs.title: Reference: Python API
docs.text: Auto-generated Python API documentation powered by mkdocstrings.

docs.title: nse.core.pipeline
docs.text: Test pipeline: orchestrates a single NSE test run.

docs.title: The oracle contract
docs.text:
A firewall test is a negative assertion ("this packet did not get through"), and a negative assertion is worthless unless the instrument is known to be working. So every run carries its own positive control: a canary packet is injected before the test packets and again after them, and the run is only reported as a result if the kernel trace for both canaries was observed.

  • The pre-canary replaces the old readiness probe, which signalled that this process had scheduled its read loop — not that nft monitor trace had actually subscribed to the kernel. Packets injected in that window were lost.
  • The post-canary proves the monitor was still watching when the last test packet went in. It is what catches a trace deadline expiring mid-run, which used to silently truncate the verdict stream.

If either canary is not observed the pipeline emits an error event and the caller fails the test. It is never possible for this pipeline to report a clean verdict list that it did not actually measure.

docs.title: run_test_pipeline(request, controller=None, queue=None, run=None) async
docs.text:
Full test lifecycle coroutine.

Executes a test request in isolated Linux network namespaces, injecting packets and collecting kernel nftables trace events.

The returned list never contains canary events: they are the pipeline's own instrument check, not part of the user's test. If a canary is missed, the list contains an error event instead of a verdict stream, so a caller cannot mistake "the oracle saw nothing" for "nothing happened".

:func:run_test_pipeline_report runs the same experiment and returns the full :class:~nse.models.experiment_report.ExperimentReport instead.

Source code in nse/core/pipeline.py 
async def run_test_pipeline(
    request: TestRequest,
    controller: NetnsController | None = None,
    queue: asyncio.Queue[TraceEvent | None] | None = None,
    run: TestRun | None = None,
) -> list[TraceEvent]:
    """
    Full test lifecycle coroutine.

    Executes a test request in isolated Linux network namespaces, injecting
    packets and collecting kernel nftables trace events.

    The returned list never contains canary events: they are the pipeline's own
    instrument check, not part of the user's test. If a canary is missed, the
    list contains an ``error`` event instead of a verdict stream, so a caller
    cannot mistake "the oracle saw nothing" for "nothing happened".

    :func:`run_test_pipeline_report` runs the same experiment and returns the
    full :class:`~nse.models.experiment_report.ExperimentReport` instead.
    """
    experiment = await _execute(
        request, controller or NetnsController(), run or _new_run(request, queue), None
    )
    if experiment.teardown_error is not None:
        raise experiment.teardown_error  # as before: a failed teardown is never silent
    return experiment.user_events()

docs.title: run_test_pipeline_report(request, controller=None, queue=None, run=None, *, timeout=None) async
docs.text:
Run the experiment of :func:run_test_pipeline and return its full report.

The same implementation runs; only the result differs. Errors do not raise: setup, rule, oracle, execution and teardown failures are recorded with their stage, and result.outcome tells them apart. With timeout, a run still going after that many seconds is stopped (outcome="timeout") and torn down. Cancellation still propagates.

Source code in nse/core/pipeline.py 
async def run_test_pipeline_report(
    request: TestRequest,
    controller: NetnsController | None = None,
    queue: asyncio.Queue[TraceEvent | None] | None = None,
    run: TestRun | None = None,
    *,
    timeout: float | None = None,
) -> ExperimentReport:
    """
    Run the experiment of :func:`run_test_pipeline` and return its full report.

    The same implementation runs; only the result differs. Errors do not
    raise: setup, rule, oracle, execution and teardown failures are recorded
    with their stage, and ``result.outcome`` tells them apart. With *timeout*,
    a run still going after that many seconds is stopped (``outcome="timeout"``)
    and torn down. Cancellation still propagates.
    """
    controller = controller or NetnsController()
    experiment = await _execute(request, controller, run or _new_run(request, queue), timeout)
    return _build_report(experiment, controller)

docs.title: Netns Controller
docs.text: create_namespace(..., isolated_host=True) puts the host end in its own namespace; see the host endpoint.

docs.title: nse.core.netns_controller
docs.text:
NetnsController: manages ephemeral Linux network namespaces.

All subprocess calls use iproute2 (ip) and must be run as root.

docs.title: NamespaceSandbox
docs.text:
Represents an active isolated network namespace sandbox. Provides utility methods to execute commands and inject packets inside the sandbox context.

Source code in nse/core/netns_controller.py 
class NamespaceSandbox:
    """
    Represents an active isolated network namespace sandbox.
    Provides utility methods to execute commands and inject packets inside the sandbox context.
    """

    def __init__(
        self, controller: NetnsController, name: str, *, ext_netns: str | None = None
    ) -> None:
        self.controller = controller
        self.name = name
        # We derive interface names from the sandbox name
        self.ext_iface = f"vhr-{interface_suffix(name)}"
        self.peer_iface = f"vrh-{interface_suffix(name)}"
        #: Namespace holding :attr:`ext_iface`: None when it is the namespace NSE
        #: runs in, the host endpoint's own namespace with ``isolated_host=True``.
        self.ext_netns = ext_netns
        #: With ``isolated_host=True``, the host endpoint as a sandbox of its own:
        #: run a server on ``host_ip`` with ``sandbox.host.start_process()``.
        #: Its :attr:`ext_iface` is this sandbox's :attr:`peer_iface`, and back.
        self.host: NamespaceSandbox | None = None
        self._source_v4 = "10.0.1.1"
        self._source_v6 = "fd00:1::1"
        self._processes: list[ManagedProcess] = []

    async def start_process(
        self,
        argv: Sequence[str | os.PathLike[str]],
        *,
        identity: ProcessIdentity | None = None,
        env: Mapping[str, str] | None = None,
        cwd: str | os.PathLike[str] | None = None,
        stdout: Output = "capture",
        stderr: Output = "capture",
        max_output_bytes: int = DEFAULT_OUTPUT_LIMIT,
        start_timeout: float = DEFAULT_START_TIMEOUT,
    ) -> ManagedProcess:
        """
        Start a long-running program in the namespace and return its handle.

        *argv* is passed exactly, as for :meth:`exec_argv`. *identity* (UID, GID,
        groups, capabilities) is applied after entering the namespace and verified
        against what the kernel reports for the process itself before the
        program is allowed to start; a mismatch raises
        :class:`~nse.core.process.IdentityError` and nothing runs. Without
        *identity* the program runs as NSE does, and that identity is recorded.

        stdin is ``/dev/null``. *stdout*/*stderr* are ``"capture"`` (keeping at
        most *max_output_bytes*, counting the rest), ``"discard"`` or a path to
        a new file. Every process still running when the sandbox closes is
        stopped, together with anything else left in the namespace.
        """
        netns = self.controller.namespace_identity(self.name)
        if netns is None:
            raise OwnershipError(f"namespace {self.name} does not exist")
        process = await spawn_process(
            self.controller.exec_prefix(self.name),
            argv,
            netns=netns,
            identity=identity,
            env=env,
            cwd=cwd,
            stdout=stdout,
            stderr=stderr,
            max_output_bytes=max_output_bytes,
            start_timeout=start_timeout,
        )
        self._processes.append(process)
        return process

    async def run_process(
        self,
        argv: Sequence[str | os.PathLike[str]],
        *,
        timeout: float | None = None,
        grace: float = DEFAULT_GRACE,
        check: bool = False,
        **options: Any,
    ) -> ProcessResult:
        """
        Run a program to completion, as :meth:`start_process` then ``wait(timeout)``.

        When *timeout* expires the process and its group are stopped (SIGTERM,
        *grace* seconds, SIGKILL) and the result says ``termination="timeout"``.
        With *check*, a result that is not ``ok`` raises
        ``subprocess.CalledProcessError``.
        """
        process = await self.start_process(argv, **options)
        result = await process.wait(timeout, grace=grace)
        return result.check() if check else result

    async def _stop_processes(self) -> None:
        """Stop every managed process still running, in parallel."""
        processes, self._processes = self._processes, []
        results = await asyncio.gather(
            *(process.terminate() for process in processes), return_exceptions=True
        )
        for process, result in zip(processes, results, strict=True):
            if isinstance(result, BaseException):
                logger.warning("Stopping %s (pid %d) failed: %s", process.argv, process.pid, result)

    async def exec(self, command: str) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[bytes]:
        """
        Run *command* inside the namespace, split on whitespace with ``str.split()``.

        No shell is involved: quotes, escapes, globs, pipes, redirections and
        variables are **not** interpreted, and an argument cannot contain a space.
        ``exec('python3 -c "print(1)"')`` passes ``'"print(1)"'`` with its quote
        characters. Use :meth:`exec_argv` to pass each argument exactly.

        Returns ``CompletedProcess[bytes]`` with ``args`` set to the full command
        (namespace prefix included); raises ``subprocess.CalledProcessError``
        carrying stdout/stderr on a non-zero exit.
        """
        return await self._run(command.split())

    async def exec_argv(
        self, argv: Sequence[str | os.PathLike[str]]
    ) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[bytes]:
        """
        Run a program inside the namespace with exactly the given arguments.

        Each element of *argv* reaches the process as one argument, unchanged:
        spaces, quotes, empty strings, Unicode and shell metacharacters are
        literal, because no shell or splitting is involved. ``argv[0]`` is the
        program, looked up on the namespace process's ``PATH`` unless it is a path.

        Result and errors are those of :meth:`exec`. Raises ``TypeError`` for a
        bare string or a non-``str`` element and ``ValueError`` for an empty
        program name or an argument containing NUL, before anything is started.
        """
        return await self._run(_validate_argv(argv))

    async def _run(self, argv: list[str]) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[bytes]:
        cmd = self.controller.exec_prefix(self.name) + argv
        proc = await asyncio.create_subprocess_exec(
            *cmd,
            stdout=asyncio.subprocess.PIPE,
            stderr=asyncio.subprocess.PIPE,
        )
        try:
            stdout, stderr = await proc.communicate()
        except asyncio.CancelledError:
            # Do not leave the child running unobserved. Its own children stay
            # in the namespace until teardown stops everything in it; use
            # start_process() for a managed tree, identity and timeouts.
            with contextlib.suppress(ProcessLookupError):
                proc.kill()
            with contextlib.suppress(asyncio.CancelledError):
                await asyncio.shield(proc.wait())
            raise
        returncode = proc.returncode if proc.returncode is not None else 1
        if returncode != 0:
            raise subprocess.CalledProcessError(
                returncode,
                cmd,
                output=stdout,
                stderr=stderr,
            )
        return subprocess.CompletedProcess(
            args=cmd,
            returncode=returncode,
            stdout=stdout,
            stderr=stderr,
        )

    async def inject_packet(
        self,
        protocol: str,
        dst_port: int,
        dst_ip: str,
        src_ip: str | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        """
        Inject a layer 3/4 packet on the host side of the veth link targeting this namespace.
        """
        from nse.core.scapy_injector import ScapyInjector
        from nse.models.test_request import PacketSpec

        injector = ScapyInjector(use_nsenter=self.controller.use_nsenter)
        packet = PacketSpec(
            protocol=cast(Any, protocol),
            dst_port=dst_port,
            dst_ip=dst_ip,
            src_ip=src_ip or (self._source_v4 if "." in dst_ip else self._source_v6),
        )

        # Sniffing/injection scapy operations can be blocking, run in executor
        await run_blocking(
            injector.inject,
            packet,
            self.name,
            self.ext_iface,
            self.peer_iface,
            self.ext_netns,
        )

    async def beacon(self, label: str) -> Beacon:
        """Send a beacon frame from this sandbox's end of its link.

        The frame leaves :attr:`peer_iface` inside the sandbox and crosses the
        veth to :attr:`ext_iface`, where a capture sees it. Register it with
        :meth:`PCAPAsserter.expect <nse.core.sniffer.PCAPAsserter.expect>`, or
        send it with ``asserter.mark(label, via=sandbox)``, which does both.
        Raises ``OSError`` if the frame cannot be sent (no ``CAP_NET_RAW``).
        """
        from nse.core import beacons

        return await beacons.send(self.peer_iface, self.name, label)

    self,
    argv: Sequence[str | os.PathLike[str]],
    *,
    identity: ProcessIdentity | None = None,
    env: Mapping[str, str] | None = None,
    cwd: str | os.PathLike[str] | None = None,
    stdout: Output = "capture",
    stderr: Output = "capture",
    max_output_bytes: int = DEFAULT_OUTPUT_LIMIT,
    start_timeout: float = DEFAULT_START_TIMEOUT,
) -> ManagedProcess:

    Start a long-running program in the namespace and return its handle.

    *argv* is passed exactly, as for :meth:`exec_argv`. *identity* (UID, GID,
    groups, capabilities) is applied after entering the namespace and verified
    against what the kernel reports for the process itself before the
    program is allowed to start; a mismatch raises
    :class:`~nse.core.process.IdentityError` and nothing runs. Without
    *identity* the program runs as NSE does, and that identity is recorded.

    stdin is ``/dev/null``. *stdout*/*stderr* are ``"capture"`` (keeping at
    most *max_output_bytes*, counting the rest), ``"discard"`` or a path to
    a new file. Every process still running when the sandbox closes is
    stopped, together with anything else left in the namespace.
    """

    if netns is None:
        raise OwnershipError(f"namespace {self.name} does not exist")

        self.controller.exec_prefix(self.name),
        argv,
        netns=netns,
        identity=identity,
        env=env,
        cwd=cwd,
        stdout=stdout,
        stderr=stderr,
        max_output_bytes=max_output_bytes,
        start_timeout=start_timeout,
    )
    self._processes.append(process)
    return process

class NetnsController:
    """
    Central orchestrator for network namespace lifecycle and test management.
    """

    def __init__(self, use_nsenter: bool | None = None) -> None:
        self._active_ns: set[str] = set()  # namespace names
        if use_nsenter is None:
            self.use_nsenter = is_in_container()
        else:
            self.use_nsenter = use_nsenter
        self._registry = ResourceRegistry()
        self._resources = NetworkResources(self.use_nsenter)
        self._runs: dict[str, str] = {}
        self.startup_sweep()

    def startup_sweep(self) -> None:
        """Recover verified abandoned ownership journals; preserve unmarked resources."""
        try:
            self._registry.recover(self._cleanup_resources)
            for name in self._resources.unmarked():
                logger.warning(
                    "Unmarked NSE resource %s left untouched; ownership is unknown", name
                )
        except (OSError, ValueError, OwnershipError, subprocess.SubprocessError) as exc:
            logger.warning("NSE startup recovery incomplete; resources preserved: %s", exc)

    def _cleanup_resources(
        self, journal: Journal, namespace: str | None = None, run_id: str | None = None
    ) -> None:
        # Delete links before namespace names: a process may keep an unnamed
        # namespace alive. Routes attached to a deleted link disappear with it.
        links = [
            entry
            for entry in reversed(journal.data.resources)
            if entry.kind == "link"
            and (run_id is None or entry.run_id == run_id)
            and (namespace is None or namespace in (entry.netns, entry.peer_netns))
        ]
        for entry in links:
            self._remove_resource(journal, entry)
        namespaces = [
            entry
            for entry in reversed(journal.data.resources)
            if entry.kind == "namespace"
            and (namespace is None or entry.name == namespace)
            and (run_id is None or entry.run_id == run_id)
        ]
        for entry in namespaces:
            if any(
                link.kind == "link" and entry.name in (link.netns, link.peer_netns)
                for link in journal.data.resources
            ):
                logger.warning("Preserving namespace %s with unresolved links", entry.name)
                continue
            if (
                self._remove_resource(journal, entry)
                and journal.data.owner_id == self._registry.owner_id
            ):
                self._active_ns.discard(entry.name)
                self._runs.pop(entry.name, None)

    @contextlib.contextmanager
    def _transaction(self, namespaces: Sequence[str], run_id: str) -> Iterator[None]:
        """Reserve all names and serialize preflight/setup against other NSE owners."""
        with self._registry.edit() as journal:
            if len(set(namespaces)) != len(namespaces):
                raise OwnershipError("a topology requires distinct namespace names")
            for name in namespaces:
                # Validate before either reserving or issuing a kernel command.
                Resource(kind="namespace", name=name, run_id=run_id)
                if name in self._runs or self._resources.namespace_exists(name):
                    raise OwnershipError(f"namespace {name} is already active or reserved")
            for name in namespaces:
                self._runs[name] = run_id
            try:
                yield
            except BaseException:
                self._cleanup_resources(journal, run_id=run_id)
                raise
            finally:
                for name in namespaces:
                    if not any(entry.run_id == run_id for entry in journal.data.resources):
                        self._runs.pop(name, None)

    def _cleanup_run(self, run_id: str) -> None:
        if self._registry.data is not None:
            with self._registry.edit() as journal:
                self._cleanup_resources(journal, run_id=run_id)

    def residual_resources(self, run_id: str) -> list[str]:
        """Resources of run *run_id* still recorded as owned, e.g. after a failed teardown.

        Cleanup keeps the record of anything it could not remove or verify, so a
        non-empty answer means the run did not clean up completely.
        """
        data = self._registry.data
        if data is None:
            return []
        return sorted(
            f"{entry.kind} {entry.name}" for entry in data.resources if entry.run_id == run_id
        )

    def _preflight(self, interfaces: Sequence[str], addresses: Sequence[str]) -> None:
        if len(set(interfaces)) != len(interfaces) or any(
            not name or len(name.encode()) > 15 or any(c in name for c in "/: \t\n")
            for name in interfaces
        ):
            raise ValueError("interface names must be distinct and fit Linux's 15 byte limit")
        existing = {link.ifname for link in self._resources.links(None)}
        if existing.intersection(interfaces):
            raise OwnershipError(
                f"host interface name conflict: {sorted(existing.intersection(interfaces))}"
            )
        networks = [ip_interface(address).network for address in addresses]
        for version in (4, 6):
            for route in self._resources.routes(version):
                if not route.dst or route.dst == "default":
                    continue
                destination = ip_network(route.dst, strict=False)
                if destination.prefixlen == 0:
                    continue
                for network in networks:
                    if network.version == destination.version and network.overlaps(destination):
                        raise OwnershipError(
                            f"subnet {network} conflicts with host route {destination} on {route.dev}"
                        )

    def _setup_topology(self, names: NamespaceNames, request: TestRequest, run_id: str) -> None:
        from nse.models.test_request import TopologyType

        if request.topology == TopologyType.GATEWAY:
            config = request.network or GatewayNetwork()
            assert isinstance(config, GatewayNetwork)
            with self._transaction((names.router_ns, names.server_ns), run_id):
                self._preflight(
                    (names.veth_host, names.veth_router_host),
                    (config.host_v4, config.host_v6, config.server_v4, config.server_v6),
                )
                self._configure_gateway(
                    names.router_ns,
                    names.server_ns,
                    names.veth_host,
                    names.veth_router_host,
                    names.veth_router_server,
                    names.veth_server,
                    config,
                )
        else:
            config_simple = request.network or SimpleNetwork()
            assert isinstance(config_simple, SimpleNetwork)
            with self._transaction((names.netns,), run_id):
                self._preflight(
                    (names.veth_host, names.veth_router_host),
                    (config_simple.host_v4, config_simple.host_v6),
                )
                self.create_netns(names.netns)
                self.create_veth_pair(
                    names.netns,
                    names.veth_host,
                    names.veth_router_host,
                    [config_simple.host_v4, config_simple.host_v6],
                    [config_simple.peer_v4, config_simple.peer_v6],
                )

    def _remove_resource(self, journal: Journal, entry: Resource) -> bool:
        try:
            observation = self._resources.inspect(entry, journal.marker(entry))
            if observation.status == "foreign":
                logger.warning(
                    "Preserving %s %s: ownership marker or identity differs", entry.kind, entry.name
                )
                return False
            if observation.status == "owned":
                if entry.kind == "namespace":
                    if not self._delete_namespace(entry.name):
                        return False
                else:
                    _run(
                        [
                            *self._resources.prefix(observation.netns),
                            resolve("ip"),
                            "link",
                            "del",
                            observation.name,
                        ]
                    )
            journal.discard(entry)
            return True
        except (OSError, ValueError, OwnershipError, subprocess.SubprocessError) as exc:
            logger.warning("Preserving unresolved %s %s: %s", entry.kind, entry.name, exc)
            return False

    def _cleanup_link(self, name: str) -> None:
        if self._registry.data is None:
            return
        with self._registry.edit() as journal:
            for entry in list(journal.data.resources):
                if entry.kind == "link" and name in (entry.name, entry.peer):
                    self._remove_resource(journal, entry)

    def _create_owned_pair(
        self, first: str, peer: str, peer_netns: str, first_netns: str | None = None
    ) -> None:
        with self._registry.edit() as journal:
            first_identity = self._resources.identity(first_netns)
            peer_identity = self._resources.identity(peer_netns)
            if first_identity is None or peer_identity is None:
                raise OwnershipError("cannot identify the namespaces owning the veth endpoints")
            entry = journal.add(
                Resource(
                    kind="link",
                    name=first,
                    peer=peer,
                    run_id=self._runs.setdefault(peer_netns, uuid.uuid4().hex),
                    netns=first_netns,
                    netns_identity=first_identity,
                    peer_netns=peer_netns,
                    peer_identity=peer_identity,
                )
            )
            marker = journal.marker(entry)
            # Some kernels ignore IFLA_IFALIAS during veth creation. The two MACs
            # are atomic creation attributes; a pending intent can be recovered
            # only if BOTH addresses and their peer relationship still match.
            first_mac, peer_mac = entry.mac_addresses()
            _run(
                [
                    *self._resources.prefix(first_netns),
                    resolve("ip"),
                    "link",
                    "add",
                    first,
                    "address",
                    first_mac,
                    "type",
                    "veth",
                    "peer",
                    "name",
                    peer,
                    "address",
                    peer_mac,
                ]
            )
            for interface in (first, peer):
                _run(
                    [
                        *self._resources.prefix(first_netns),
                        resolve("ip"),
                        "link",
                        "set",
                        "dev",
                        interface,
                        "alias",
                        marker,
                    ]
                )
            entry.state = "created"
            if self._resources.inspect(entry, marker).status != "owned":
                entry.state = "pending"
                raise OwnershipError("cannot confirm ownership markers on the new veth pair")
            journal.save()

    def _create_owned_route(self, command: list[str], interface: str) -> None:
        with self._registry.edit() as journal:
            parent = next(
                entry
                for entry in journal.data.resources
                if entry.kind == "link" and entry.name == interface
            )
            entry = journal.add(
                Resource(
                    kind="route",
                    name=f"route_{uuid.uuid4().hex}",
                    run_id=parent.run_id,
                    parent=parent.token,
                    route=tuple(command),
                )
            )
            _run(command)
            entry.state = "created"
            journal.save()

    def namespace_identity(self, name: str) -> NetnsIdentity | None:
        """``(st_dev, st_ino)`` of namespace *name*, or None if it does not exist."""
        return self._resources.identity(name)

    def exec_prefix(self, name: str) -> list[str]:
        if self.use_nsenter:
            return [resolve("nsenter"), f"--net=/var/run/netns/{name}", "--"]
        else:
            return [resolve("ip"), "netns", "exec", name]

    def _run_in_netns(self, name: str, cmd: list[str]) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]:
        return _run(self.exec_prefix(name) + cmd)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Namespace lifecycle
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def create_netns(self, name: str) -> None:
        """Create a new network namespace. Raises on failure."""
        logger.debug("Creating netns: %s", name)
        with self._registry.edit() as journal:
            if any(
                entry.kind == "namespace" and entry.name == name for entry in journal.data.resources
            ):
                raise OwnershipError(f"namespace {name} is already registered by this controller")
            entry = journal.add(
                Resource(
                    kind="namespace",
                    name=name,
                    run_id=self._runs.setdefault(name, uuid.uuid4().hex),
                )
            )
            _run([resolve("ip"), "netns", "add", name])
            self._active_ns.add(name)
            entry.identity = self._resources.identity(name)
            if entry.identity is None:
                raise OwnershipError(f"cannot confirm identity of newly created namespace {name}")
            try:
                self._run_in_netns(
                    name,
                    [resolve("ip"), "link", "set", "dev", "lo", "alias", journal.marker(entry)],
                )
            except BaseException:
                # Live rollback has the successful exclusive creation and its
                # inode as evidence. Crash recovery still requires the marker.
                try:
                    unclaimed = all(not link.ifalias for link in self._resources.links(name))
                except Exception:
                    # Entering the namespace is what failed (e.g. `ip netns exec`
                    # in some containers). The exclusive creation under the
                    # registry lock and the unchanged inode remain the evidence;
                    # the original error, not this one, is re-raised below.
                    unclaimed = True
                if (
                    self._resources.identity(name) == entry.identity
                    and unclaimed
                    and self._delete_namespace(name)
                ):
                    journal.discard(entry)
                    self._active_ns.discard(name)
                raise
            if self._resources.inspect(entry, journal.marker(entry)).status != "owned":
                raise OwnershipError(f"cannot confirm ownership marker of namespace {name}")
            entry.state = "created"
            journal.save()
        # Disable DAD inside the netns to speed up IPv6 interface readiness
        try:
            self._run_in_netns(
                name,
                [
                    resolve("sysctl"),
                    "-w",
                    "net.ipv6.conf.all.accept_dad=0",
                ],
            )
            self._run_in_netns(
                name,
                [
                    resolve("sysctl"),
                    "-w",
                    "net.ipv6.conf.default.accept_dad=0",
                ],
            )
        except subprocess.CalledProcessError as e:
            logger.warning("Could not set accept_dad sysctls inside netns %s: %s", name, e)

    def destroy_netns(self, name: str) -> None:
        """Remove only this controller's verified namespace and associated links."""
        if self._registry.data is None:
            logger.warning("Namespace %s is not owned by this controller; left untouched", name)
            return
        with self._registry.edit() as journal:
            if not any(
                entry.kind == "namespace" and entry.name == name for entry in journal.data.resources
            ):
                logger.warning("Namespace %s is not owned by this controller; left untouched", name)
                return
            self._cleanup_resources(journal, namespace=name)

    def _delete_namespace(self, name: str) -> bool:
        # The namespace is the process boundary: nothing started in it, nor
        # anything those processes left behind (even detached from their
        # session), may outlive it unseen in an unnamed namespace.
        netns = self._resources.identity(name)
        if netns is not None:
            try:
                survivors = terminate_namespace(netns)
            except ProtectedNamespaceError as exc:
                logger.error("Not deleting namespace %s: %s", name, exc)
                return False
            if survivors:
                logger.warning(
                    "Processes %s survived SIGKILL in namespace %s; deleting it anyway",
                    survivors,
                    name,
                )
        delays = [0.1, 0.5, 1.0]
        for idx, delay in enumerate(delays):
            try:
                _run([resolve("ip"), "netns", "del", name])
                return True
            except subprocess.CalledProcessError as err:
                if "No such file or directory" in (err.stderr or ""):
                    return True
                if idx < len(delays) - 1:
                    time.sleep(delay)
                else:
                    logger.warning("Failed to destroy netns %s after 3 attempts: %s", name, err)
            except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
                logger.warning("Timeout destroying netns %s", name)
                break
        return False

    @contextlib.asynccontextmanager
    async def create_namespace(
        self,
        name: str,
        host_ip: str | list[str] = "10.0.1.1/24",
        peer_ip: str | list[str] = "10.0.1.2/24",
        *,
        isolated_host: bool = False,
    ) -> AsyncIterator[NamespaceSandbox]:
        """
        Context manager to safely construct and teardown an isolated namespace.

        By default the host end of the veth pair, with *host_ip*, is in the
        namespace NSE runs in, so traffic from the sandbox to *host_ip* crosses
        the host's own firewall; NSE logs a warning when that firewall may filter
        it. With *isolated_host*, the host end goes into a namespace of its own,
        ``nsh_<name>`` (:attr:`NamespaceSandbox.ext_netns`), created and removed
        with the sandbox: no host rule, route or firewall is on the path, and
        *host_ip* may overlap a host subnet. Run programs there through
        :attr:`NamespaceSandbox.host` and capture there with
        ``PCAPAsserter(iface=sandbox.ext_iface, netns=sandbox.ext_netns)``.
        """
        host_ns = f"nsh_{name}" if isolated_host else None
        sandbox = NamespaceSandbox(self, name, ext_netns=host_ns)

        run_id = uuid.uuid4().hex

        def setup() -> None:
            namespaces = (name,) if host_ns is None else (name, host_ns)
            with self._transaction(namespaces, run_id):
                self._preflight(
                    (sandbox.ext_iface, sandbox.peer_iface),
                    # An isolated endpoint shares no routing table with the host.
                    (config.host_v4, config.host_v6) if host_ns is None else (),
                )
                sandbox._source_v4 = str(ip_interface(config.host_v4).ip)
                sandbox._source_v6 = str(ip_interface(config.host_v6).ip)
                self.create_netns(name)
                if host_ns is None:
                    self.create_veth_pair(
                        name, sandbox.ext_iface, sandbox.peer_iface, host_ip, peer_ip
                    )
                    return
                self.create_netns(host_ns)
                self._configure_pair(
                    name, sandbox.ext_iface, sandbox.peer_iface, config, host_netns=host_ns
                )
                view = NamespaceSandbox(self, host_ns, ext_netns=name)
                view.ext_iface, view.peer_iface = sandbox.peer_iface, sandbox.ext_iface
                view._source_v4 = str(ip_interface(config.peer_v4).ip)
                view._source_v6 = str(ip_interface(config.peer_v6).ip)
                sandbox.host = view

        config = self._simple_network(host_ip, peer_ip)
        try:
            await run_blocking(setup)
            if host_ns is None:
                await run_blocking(warn_if_filtered, name, [config.host_v4, config.host_v6])
            yield sandbox
        finally:
            try:
                await asyncio.gather(
                    sandbox._stop_processes(),
                    *([sandbox.host._stop_processes()] if sandbox.host else []),
                )
            finally:
                await run_blocking(self._cleanup_run, run_id)

    @staticmethod
    def _simple_network(host_ip: str | list[str], peer_ip: str | list[str]) -> SimpleNetwork:
        addresses = {}
        for label, value in (("host", host_ip), ("peer", peer_ip)):
            for address in [value] if isinstance(value, str) else value:
                family = ip_interface(address).version
                key = f"{label}_v{family}"
                if key in addresses:
                    raise ValueError("at most one address per family is supported on each endpoint")
                addresses[key] = address
        return SimpleNetwork(**addresses)

    def create_veth_pair(
        self,
        netns_name: str,
        veth_host: str,
        veth_peer: str,
        host_ip: str | list[str] = "10.0.0.1/24",
        peer_ip: str | list[str] = "10.0.0.2/24",
    ) -> None:
        """
        Create a veth pair, move one end into *netns_name*, and assign IPs.
        """
        config = self._simple_network(host_ip, peer_ip)
        with self._registry.edit() as journal:
            self._preflight((veth_host, veth_peer), (config.host_v4, config.host_v6))
            before = {entry.token for entry in journal.data.resources}
            try:
                self._configure_pair(netns_name, veth_host, veth_peer, config)
            except BaseException:
                for entry in reversed(list(journal.data.resources)):
                    if entry.kind == "link" and entry.token not in before:
                        self._remove_resource(journal, entry)
                raise

    def _configure_pair(
        self,
        netns_name: str,
        veth_host: str,
        veth_peer: str,
        config: SimpleNetwork,
        host_netns: str | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        v4_host, v6_host = config.host_v4, config.host_v6
        v4_peer, v6_peer = config.peer_v4, config.peer_v6
        # Commands for the host end run where it lives: NSE's own namespace, or
        # the isolated host endpoint's.
        host = self._resources.prefix(host_netns)

        # Create the veth pair on the host side
        self._create_owned_pair(veth_host, veth_peer, netns_name, host_netns)
        # Move the peer end into the target namespace
        _run([*host, resolve("ip"), "link", "set", veth_peer, "netns", netns_name])

        # --- Host side ---
        if v4_host:
            _run([*host, resolve("ip"), "addr", "add", v4_host, "dev", veth_host])
        if v6_host:
            _run([*host, resolve("ip"), "addr", "add", v6_host, "dev", veth_host])
        _run([*host, resolve("ip"), "link", "set", veth_host, "up"])
        if host_netns is not None:
            _run([*host, resolve("ip"), "link", "set", "lo", "up"])

        # --- Namespace side ---
        if v4_peer:
            self._run_in_netns(
                netns_name,
                [
                    resolve("ip"),
                    "addr",
                    "add",
                    v4_peer,
                    "dev",
                    veth_peer,
                ],
            )
        if v6_peer:
            self._run_in_netns(
                netns_name,
                [
                    resolve("ip"),
                    "addr",
                    "add",
                    v6_peer,
                    "dev",
                    veth_peer,
                ],
            )
        self._run_in_netns(netns_name, [resolve("ip"), "link", "set", veth_peer, "up"])
        self._run_in_netns(netns_name, [resolve("ip"), "link", "set", "lo", "up"])

    def create_gateway_topology(
        self,
        router_ns: str,
        server_ns: str,
        veth_host: str,
        veth_router_host: str,
        veth_router_server: str,
        veth_server: str,
        host_v4: str = "10.0.1.1/24",
        router_host_v4: str = "10.0.1.2/24",
        router_server_v4: str = "10.0.2.1/24",
        server_v4: str = "10.0.2.2/24",
        host_v6: str = "fd00:1::1/64",
        router_host_v6: str = "fd00:1::2/64",
        router_server_v6: str = "fd00:2::1/64",
        server_v6: str = "fd00:2::2/64",
    ) -> None:
        """
        Create router and server namespaces, build double veth links,
        enable IPv4/IPv6 forwarding inside the router, and add transit routes.
        """
        config = GatewayNetwork(
            host_v4=host_v4,
            router_host_v4=router_host_v4,
            router_server_v4=router_server_v4,
            server_v4=server_v4,
            host_v6=host_v6,
            router_host_v6=router_host_v6,
            router_server_v6=router_server_v6,
            server_v6=server_v6,
        )
        with self._transaction((router_ns, server_ns), uuid.uuid4().hex):
            self._preflight((veth_host, veth_router_host), (host_v4, host_v6, server_v4, server_v6))
            self._configure_gateway(
                router_ns,
                server_ns,
                veth_host,
                veth_router_host,
                veth_router_server,
                veth_server,
                config,
            )

    def _configure_gateway(
        self,
        router_ns: str,
        server_ns: str,
        veth_host: str,
        veth_router_host: str,
        veth_router_server: str,
        veth_server: str,
        config: GatewayNetwork,
    ) -> None:
        host_v4, host_v6 = config.host_v4, config.host_v6
        router_host_v4, router_host_v6 = config.router_host_v4, config.router_host_v6
        router_server_v4, router_server_v6 = config.router_server_v4, config.router_server_v6
        server_v4, server_v6 = config.server_v4, config.server_v6
        if len({veth_router_host, veth_router_server, veth_server}) != 3:
            raise ValueError("gateway interfaces must have distinct names")
        # Validate the second pair too before creating either namespace.
        self._preflight((veth_router_server, veth_server), ())
        # Create namespaces
        self.create_netns(router_ns)
        self.create_netns(server_ns)

        # Enable IPv4/IPv6 forwarding on router namespace
        self._run_in_netns(router_ns, [resolve("sysctl"), "-w", "net.ipv4.ip_forward=1"])
        self._run_in_netns(
            router_ns,
            [
                resolve("sysctl"),
                "-w",
                "net.ipv6.conf.all.forwarding=1",
            ],
        )

        # 1. Create Host <-> Router veth pair
        self._create_owned_pair(veth_host, veth_router_host, router_ns)
        _run([resolve("ip"), "link", "set", veth_router_host, "netns", router_ns])

        _run([resolve("ip"), "addr", "add", host_v4, "dev", veth_host])
        _run([resolve("ip"), "addr", "add", host_v6, "dev", veth_host])
        _run([resolve("ip"), "link", "set", veth_host, "up"])

        self._run_in_netns(
            router_ns,
            [
                resolve("ip"),
                "addr",
                "add",
                router_host_v4,
                "dev",
                veth_router_host,
            ],
        )
        self._run_in_netns(
            router_ns,
            [
                resolve("ip"),
                "addr",
                "add",
                router_host_v6,
                "dev",
                veth_router_host,
            ],
        )
        self._run_in_netns(
            router_ns,
            [
                resolve("ip"),
                "link",
                "set",
                veth_router_host,
                "up",
            ],
        )

        # 2. Create Router <-> Server veth pair
        self._create_owned_pair(veth_router_server, veth_server, server_ns, router_ns)
        self._run_in_netns(
            router_ns,
            [
                resolve("ip"),
                "link",
                "set",
                veth_server,
                "netns",
                server_ns,
            ],
        )

        self._run_in_netns(
            router_ns,
            [
                resolve("ip"),
                "addr",
                "add",
                router_server_v4,
                "dev",
                veth_router_server,
            ],
        )
        self._run_in_netns(
            router_ns,
            [
                resolve("ip"),
                "addr",
                "add",
                router_server_v6,
                "dev",
                veth_router_server,
            ],
        )
        self._run_in_netns(
            router_ns,
            [
                resolve("ip"),
                "link",
                "set",
                veth_router_server,
                "up",
            ],
        )

        self._run_in_netns(
            server_ns,
            [
                resolve("ip"),
                "addr",
                "add",
                server_v4,
                "dev",
                veth_server,
            ],
        )
        self._run_in_netns(
            server_ns,
            [
                resolve("ip"),
                "addr",
                "add",
                server_v6,
                "dev",
                veth_server,
            ],
        )
        self._run_in_netns(server_ns, [resolve("ip"), "link", "set", veth_server, "up"])

        # Bring up loopbacks
        self._run_in_netns(router_ns, [resolve("ip"), "link", "set", "lo", "up"])
        self._run_in_netns(server_ns, [resolve("ip"), "link", "set", "lo", "up"])

        # 3. Setup transit routing
        # Route on Host: Server subnet via Router host IP
        host_rt_via = router_host_v4.split("/")[0]
        host_rt_via6 = router_host_v6.split("/")[0]
        self._create_owned_route(
            [
                resolve("ip"),
                "route",
                "add",
                str(ip_interface(server_v4).network),
                "via",
                host_rt_via,
                "dev",
                veth_host,
            ],
            veth_host,
        )
        self._create_owned_route(
            [
                resolve("ip"),
                "-6",
                "route",
                "add",
                str(ip_interface(server_v6).network),
                "via",
                host_rt_via6,
                "dev",
                veth_host,
            ],
            veth_host,
        )

        # Route on Server: Host subnet via Router server IP (default route is cleanest)
        srv_rt_via = router_server_v4.split("/")[0]
        srv_rt_via6 = router_server_v6.split("/")[0]
        self._run_in_netns(
            server_ns,
            [
                resolve("ip"),
                "route",
                "add",
                "default",
                "via",
                srv_rt_via,
                "dev",
                veth_server,
            ],
        )
        self._run_in_netns(
            server_ns,
            [
                resolve("ip"),
                "-6",
                "route",
                "add",
                "default",
                "via",
                srv_rt_via6,
                "dev",
                veth_server,
            ],
        )

    def cleanup_all(self) -> None:
        """
        Destroy this controller's verified resources. Called on SIGINT/SIGTERM.
        Safe to call multiple times.
        """
        logger.info("Cleaning up %d namespace(s)…", len(self._active_ns))
        if self._registry.data is not None:
            with self._registry.edit() as journal:
                self._cleanup_resources(journal)

    self,
    name: str,
    host_ip: str | list[str] = "10.0.1.1/24",
    peer_ip: str | list[str] = "10.0.1.2/24",
    *,
    isolated_host: bool = False,
) -> AsyncIterator[NamespaceSandbox]:

    Context manager to safely construct and teardown an isolated namespace.

    By default the host end of the veth pair, with *host_ip*, is in the
    namespace NSE runs in, so traffic from the sandbox to *host_ip* crosses
    the host's own firewall; NSE logs a warning when that firewall may filter
    it. With *isolated_host*, the host end goes into a namespace of its own,
    ``nsh_<name>`` (:attr:`NamespaceSandbox.ext_netns`), created and removed

    :attr:`NamespaceSandbox.host` and capture there with
    ``PCAPAsserter(iface=sandbox.ext_iface, netns=sandbox.ext_netns)``.
    """

                (sandbox.ext_iface, sandbox.peer_iface),
                # An isolated endpoint shares no routing table with the host.
                (config.host_v4, config.host_v6) if host_ns is None else (),
            )

            sandbox._source_v6 = str(ip_interface(config.host_v6).ip)

            if host_ns is None:
                self.create_veth_pair(
                    name, sandbox.ext_iface, sandbox.peer_iface, host_ip, peer_ip
                )
                return
            self.create_netns(host_ns)
            self._configure_pair(
                name, sandbox.ext_iface, sandbox.peer_iface, config, host_netns=host_ns
            )

            view.ext_iface, view.peer_iface = sandbox.peer_iface, sandbox.ext_iface

Source code in nse/core/netns_controller.py 
def create_netns(self, name: str) -> None:
    """Create a new network namespace. Raises on failure."""
    logger.debug("Creating netns: %s", name)
    with self._registry.edit() as journal:
        if any(
            entry.kind == "namespace" and entry.name == name for entry in journal.data.resources
        ):
            raise OwnershipError(f"namespace {name} is already registered by this controller")
        entry = journal.add(
            Resource(
                kind="namespace",
                name=name,
                run_id=self._runs.setdefault(name, uuid.uuid4().hex),
            )
        )
        _run([resolve("ip"), "netns", "add", name])
        self._active_ns.add(name)
        entry.identity = self._resources.identity(name)
        if entry.identity is None:
            raise OwnershipError(f"cannot confirm identity of newly created namespace {name}")
        try:
            self._run_in_netns(
                name,
                [resolve("ip"), "link", "set", "dev", "lo", "alias", journal.marker(entry)],
            )
        except BaseException:
            # Live rollback has the successful exclusive creation and its
            # inode as evidence. Crash recovery still requires the marker.
            try:
                unclaimed = all(not link.ifalias for link in self._resources.links(name))
            except Exception:
                # Entering the namespace is what failed (e.g. `ip netns exec`
                # in some containers). The exclusive creation under the
                # registry lock and the unchanged inode remain the evidence;
                # the original error, not this one, is re-raised below.
                unclaimed = True
            if (
                self._resources.identity(name) == entry.identity
                and unclaimed
                and self._delete_namespace(name)
            ):
                journal.discard(entry)
                self._active_ns.discard(name)
            raise
        if self._resources.inspect(entry, journal.marker(entry)).status != "owned":
            raise OwnershipError(f"cannot confirm ownership marker of namespace {name}")
        entry.state = "created"
        journal.save()
    # Disable DAD inside the netns to speed up IPv6 interface readiness
    try:
        self._run_in_netns(
            name,
            [
                resolve("sysctl"),
                "-w",
                "net.ipv6.conf.all.accept_dad=0",
            ],
        )
        self._run_in_netns(
            name,
            [
                resolve("sysctl"),
                "-w",
                "net.ipv6.conf.default.accept_dad=0",
            ],
        )
    except subprocess.CalledProcessError as e:
        logger.warning("Could not set accept_dad sysctls inside netns %s: %s", name, e)

def create_veth_pair(
    self,
    netns_name: str,
    veth_host: str,
    veth_peer: str,
    host_ip: str | list[str] = "10.0.0.1/24",
    peer_ip: str | list[str] = "10.0.0.2/24",
) -> None:
    """
    Create a veth pair, move one end into *netns_name*, and assign IPs.
    """
    config = self._simple_network(host_ip, peer_ip)
    with self._registry.edit() as journal:
        self._preflight((veth_host, veth_peer), (config.host_v4, config.host_v6))
        before = {entry.token for entry in journal.data.resources}
        try:
            self._configure_pair(netns_name, veth_host, veth_peer, config)
        except BaseException:
            for entry in reversed(list(journal.data.resources)):
                if entry.kind == "link" and entry.token not in before:
                    self._remove_resource(journal, entry)
            raise

def residual_resources(self, run_id: str) -> list[str]:
    """Resources of run *run_id* still recorded as owned, e.g. after a failed teardown.

    Cleanup keeps the record of anything it could not remove or verify, so a
    non-empty answer means the run did not clean up completely.
    """
    data = self._registry.data
    if data is None:
        return []
    return sorted(
        f"{entry.kind} {entry.name}" for entry in data.resources if entry.run_id == run_id
    )

docs.text: Read once per process by create_namespace() in the default topology. It only warns; it never fails a setup.

docs.title: nse.core.host_firewall
docs.text:
Detect a host firewall that can filter traffic from a sandbox to its host endpoint.

In the simple topology the host end of the veth pair, with host_ip, lives in the namespace NSE runs in. Traffic from the sandbox to host_ip is therefore local input for that namespace and crosses its firewall (firewalld, ufw, a hand-written nftables ruleset). A test server listening on host_ip then never sees a request the host dropped, and the test reads the silence as the rules under test blocking it.

The check reads the ruleset once per process with nft -j list ruleset and reports the input hooks that drop by policy or reach an unconditional drop/reject. It cannot know which port a test uses, nor whether an earlier accept already admits it, so it can only say may filter; it never fails a setup. iptables-legacy rules are invisible to nft and are not inspected.

def host_input_filters() -> list[str]:
    """The filtering input hooks of the host's ruleset, read once per process.

    Empty when nothing filters, and also when the ruleset cannot be read (no
    ``nft``, no permission): this is a diagnostic, not a guarantee.
    """
    global _findings
    if _findings is None:
        try:
            nft = resolve_optional("nft")
            if nft is None:
                _findings = []
                return _findings
            result = subprocess.run(
                [nft, "-j", "list", "ruleset"],
                capture_output=True,
                text=True,
                check=True,
                timeout=5.0,
            )
            _findings = input_filters(json.loads(result.stdout or "{}"))
        except Exception as exc:  # a diagnostic must never break a setup
            logger.debug("Host firewall not inspected: %s", exc)
            _findings = []
    return _findings

docs.text:
Describe the input hooks in an nft -j list ruleset document that filter.

Each finding names the base chain and why it filters: its policy is drop, or it reaches (directly, or through jump/goto) a rule that drops or rejects everything that gets that far.

Source code in nse/core/host_firewall.py 
def input_filters(ruleset: Any) -> list[str]:
    """Describe the input hooks in an ``nft -j list ruleset`` document that filter.

    Each finding names the base chain and why it filters: its policy is
    ``drop``, or it reaches (directly, or through ``jump``/``goto``) a rule that
    drops or rejects everything that gets that far.
    """
    items = ruleset.get("nftables", []) if isinstance(ruleset, dict) else []
    chains: dict[tuple[str, str, str], dict[str, Any]] = {}
    rules: dict[tuple[str, str, str], list[list[dict[str, Any]]]] = {}
    for item in items:
        if not isinstance(item, dict):
            continue
        if isinstance(chain := item.get("chain"), dict):
            key = (chain.get("family"), chain.get("table"), chain.get("name"))
            chains[key] = chain  # type: ignore[index]
        elif isinstance(rule := item.get("rule"), dict):
            key = (rule.get("family"), rule.get("table"), rule.get("chain"))
            expr = rule.get("expr")
            if isinstance(expr, list):
                rules.setdefault(key, []).append(expr)  # type: ignore[arg-type]

    def terminal(key: tuple[str, str, str], seen: set[tuple[str, str, str]]) -> str | None:
        if key in seen:
            return None
        seen.add(key)
        for expr in rules.get(key, []):
            statements = [next(iter(s)) for s in expr if isinstance(s, dict) and s]
            verdicts = [s for s in statements if s in _TERMINAL]
            if verdicts and all(s in _UNCONDITIONAL or s in _TERMINAL for s in statements):
                return f"{verdicts[0]} in chain {key[2]}"
            for statement in expr:
                for kind in ("jump", "goto"):
                    target = statement.get(kind) if isinstance(statement, dict) else None
                    if isinstance(target, dict) and isinstance(target.get("target"), str):
                        found = terminal((key[0], key[1], target["target"]), seen)
                        if found:
                            return found
        return None

    findings = []
    for key, chain in chains.items():
        if chain.get("hook") != "input" or key[0] not in _INPUT_FAMILIES:
            continue
        name = f"{key[0]} {key[1]} {key[2]}"
        if chain.get("policy") == "drop":
            findings.append(f"{name}: policy drop")
        elif reason := terminal(key, set()):
            findings.append(f"{name}: {reason}")
    return sorted(findings)

docs.title: warn_if_filtered(namespace, host_addresses)
docs.text:
Log, once per process, that the host firewall may filter host_addresses.

Returns True when a warning was (or had already been) issued.

Source code in nse/core/host_firewall.py 
def warn_if_filtered(namespace: str, host_addresses: list[str]) -> bool:
    """Log, once per process, that the host firewall may filter *host_addresses*.

    Returns True when a warning was (or had already been) issued.
    """
    global _warned
    findings = host_input_filters()
    if not findings:
        return False
    if not _warned:
        _warned = True
        logger.warning(
            "The host firewall may filter traffic from namespace %s to its host endpoint "
            "%s (%s). A server bound there can miss requests the host dropped, which a "
            "test would attribute to the rules under test. Pass isolated_host=True to "
            "create_namespace() to keep the host endpoint out of the host's firewall.",
            namespace,
            ", ".join(host_addresses),
            "; ".join(findings),
        )
    return True

docs.title: nse.core.process
docs.text: Managed application processes inside a network namespace.

docs.title: Launch chain
docs.text:
::

<namespace prefix> [setpriv <identity> --] sh -c PROBE nse-launch argv...
  1. The namespace prefix (ip netns exec or nsenter) enters the network namespace with NSE's own privileges.
  2. setpriv (util-linux) applies the requested identity: UID, GID, supplementary groups, capabilities. It refuses, rather than continuing, when any part cannot be applied. Nothing runs as a preexec_fn in NSE's multi-threaded process.
  3. A POSIX shell probe, which already is the final process (same PID), sends its own /proc/$$/status to NSE and blocks. NSE compares the identity the kernel reports with the request and only then lets the probe exec the application. On a mismatch the application never starts: there is no fallback to root.

The handshake runs over the chain's stdin, one end of a socketpair: the probe writes the report to descriptor 0 and reads the answer from it, then starts the application with stdin on /dev/null. Only descriptors 0-2 are involved, so it works with any POSIX sh (dash only redirects descriptors 0-9), and the application inherits none of NSE's descriptors.

docs.title: Boundary
docs.text: Each managed process leads a new session, so its process group is stopped as a unit (SIGTERM, a grace period, then SIGKILL). A descendant that leaves the group (setsid, daemonisation) is still inside the network namespace, and the namespace is the boundary NSE enforces before deleting it: :func:terminate_namespace stops every process in it. Membership is checked through a pidfd, so a recycled PID is never signalled, and crash recovery needs no PID records at all. A process that moves itself to another network namespace (which requires CAP_SYS_ADMIN) is outside this boundary.

Source code in nse/core/process.py 
class ManagedProcess:
    """A process started by :func:`spawn_process`. Stop it with :meth:`terminate`
    or ``async with``; :meth:`wait` and :meth:`terminate` return the same
    :class:`~nse.models.process.ProcessResult` however often they are called."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        *,
        proc: asyncio.subprocess.Process,
        pidfd: int | None,
        argv: list[str],
        command: list[str],
        netns: NetnsIdentity,
        identity: EffectiveIdentity,
        started_at: float,
        captures: dict[Stream, _Capture],
        paths: dict[Stream, str],
    ) -> None:
        self._proc = proc
        self._pidfd = pidfd
        self.argv = argv
        self.command = command
        self.netns = netns
        self.identity = identity
        self.started_at = started_at
        self._captures = captures
        self._paths = paths
        self._exited: asyncio.Future[int] = asyncio.ensure_future(proc.wait())
        self._termination: Termination = "exited"
        self._stop_task: asyncio.Future[ProcessResult] | None = None
        self._finish_task: asyncio.Future[ProcessResult] | None = None

    @property
    def pid(self) -> int:
        return self._proc.pid

    @property
    def returncode(self) -> int | None:
        """None while the process runs."""
        return self._proc.returncode

    def output(self, stream: Stream = "stdout") -> bytes:
        """What has been captured from *stream* so far."""
        return bytes(self._capture(stream).data)

    def output_dropped(self, stream: Stream = "stdout") -> int:
        """Bytes of *stream* discarded so far because the capture limit was reached."""
        return self._capture(stream).dropped

    def _capture(self, stream: Stream) -> _Capture:
        try:
            return self._captures[stream]
        except KeyError:
            raise ValueError(f"{stream} is not captured for this process") from None

    async def wait_for_output(
        self, marker: bytes, *, timeout: float, stream: Stream = "stdout"
    ) -> None:
        """Return once *marker* appears in the captured *stream*: an explicit readiness signal.

        Raises :class:`ProcessExitedError` if the process ends first and
        ``TimeoutError`` (leaving the process running) if *timeout* expires.
        """
        capture = self._capture(stream)
        deadline = time.monotonic() + timeout
        while marker not in capture.data:
            if self._exited.done():
                await capture.wait_eof(_OUTPUT_DRAIN)  # what it printed last may be in flight
                if marker in capture.data:
                    return
                result = await self._finish()
                raise ProcessExitedError(
                    f"process {self.argv[0]!r} exited with {result.returncode} before "
                    f"printing {marker!r}",
                    result,
                )
            remaining = deadline - time.monotonic()
            if remaining <= 0:
                raise TimeoutError(f"{marker!r} not seen on {stream} within {timeout}s")
            capture.changed.clear()
            changed: asyncio.Future[object] = asyncio.ensure_future(capture.changed.wait())
            exited: asyncio.Future[object] = asyncio.ensure_future(asyncio.shield(self._exited))
            try:
                await asyncio.wait(
                    {changed, exited}, timeout=remaining, return_when=asyncio.FIRST_COMPLETED
                )
            finally:
                changed.cancel()
                exited.cancel()

    async def wait(
        self, timeout: float | None = None, *, grace: float = DEFAULT_GRACE
    ) -> ProcessResult:
        """Wait for the process to end. If *timeout* expires, stop it (termination
        ``timeout``); if the waiting task is cancelled, stop it and re-raise."""
        try:
            await asyncio.wait_for(asyncio.shield(self._exited), timeout)
        except asyncio.TimeoutError:
            return await self._stop("timeout", grace)
        except asyncio.CancelledError:
            with contextlib.suppress(asyncio.CancelledError):
                await asyncio.shield(self._stop("cancelled", grace))
            raise
        return await self._stop("exited", grace)

    async def terminate(self, grace: float = DEFAULT_GRACE) -> ProcessResult:
        """Stop the process and its group: SIGTERM, *grace* seconds, then SIGKILL."""
        return await self._stop("terminated", grace)

    async def __aenter__(self) -> ManagedProcess:
        return self

    async def __aexit__(self, *exc_info: object) -> None:
        await self.terminate()

    def _stop(self, reason: Termination, grace: float) -> asyncio.Future[ProcessResult]:
        if self._stop_task is None:
            self._stop_task = asyncio.ensure_future(self._do_stop(reason, grace))
        return asyncio.shield(self._stop_task)

    def _signal_group(self, sig: int) -> None:
        if self._pidfd is not None and not self._exited.done():
            with contextlib.suppress(ProcessLookupError):
                pidfd_send_signal(self._pidfd, sig)
        signal_namespace(self.netns, sig, pgid=self.pid)

    async def _do_stop(self, reason: Termination, grace: float) -> ProcessResult:
        if not self._exited.done():
            self._termination = reason
            await run_blocking(self._signal_group, signal.SIGTERM)
            done, _ = await asyncio.wait({self._exited}, timeout=grace)
            if not done:
                await run_blocking(self._signal_group, signal.SIGKILL)
                await asyncio.shield(self._exited)
        if reason != "exited":
            # NSE was asked to stop it: what the leader left in its group, still
            # in the namespace, goes too. After a natural exit such members are
            # left to the namespace teardown, which stops everything in it.
            await run_blocking(signal_namespace, self.netns, signal.SIGKILL, pgid=self.pid)
        return await self._finish()

    def _finish(self) -> asyncio.Future[ProcessResult]:
        """The single finalisation, shared by every caller (stop, readiness, wait)."""
        if self._finish_task is None:
            self._finish_task = asyncio.ensure_future(self._build_result())
        return asyncio.shield(self._finish_task)

    async def _build_result(self) -> ProcessResult:
        await asyncio.shield(self._exited)
        complete = True
        for capture in self._captures.values():
            if not await capture.wait_eof(_OUTPUT_DRAIN):
                complete = False
            capture.close()
        if self._pidfd is not None:
            os.close(self._pidfd)
            self._pidfd = None
        stdout, stderr = self._captures.get("stdout"), self._captures.get("stderr")
        returncode = self._proc.returncode
        assert returncode is not None
        return ProcessResult(
            argv=self.argv,
            command=self.command,
            pid=self.pid,
            identity=self.identity,
            termination=self._termination,
            returncode=returncode,
            started_at=self.started_at,
            ended_at=time.time(),
            stdout=None if stdout is None else bytes(stdout.data),
            stderr=None if stderr is None else bytes(stderr.data),
            stdout_path=self._paths.get("stdout"),
            stderr_path=self._paths.get("stderr"),
            stdout_dropped=0 if stdout is None else stdout.dropped,
            stderr_dropped=0 if stderr is None else stderr.dropped,
            output_complete=complete,
        )

def namespace_processes(netns: NetnsIdentity, *, pgid: int | None = None) -> list[int]:
    """PIDs of the processes in network namespace *netns* (and process group *pgid*).

    Raises :class:`ProtectedNamespaceError` for NSE's own or PID 1's namespace.
    """
    _refuse_protected(netns)
    own = os.getpid()
    members = []
    for entry in os.scandir("/proc"):
        if (
            entry.name.isdigit()
            and int(entry.name) != own
            and _belongs(int(entry.name), netns, pgid)
        ):
            members.append(int(entry.name))
    return members

def signal_namespace(netns: NetnsIdentity, sig: int, *, pgid: int | None = None) -> int:
    """Signal every process in *netns* (and group *pgid*); return how many were signalled."""
    return sum(_send(pid, netns, sig, pgid) for pid in namespace_processes(netns, pgid=pgid))

async def spawn_process(
    prefix: Sequence[str],
    argv: Sequence[str | os.PathLike[str]],
    *,
    netns: NetnsIdentity,
    identity: ProcessIdentity | None = None,
    env: Mapping[str, str] | None = None,
    cwd: str | os.PathLike[str] | None = None,
    stdout: Output = "capture",
    stderr: Output = "capture",
    max_output_bytes: int = DEFAULT_OUTPUT_LIMIT,
    start_timeout: float = DEFAULT_START_TIMEOUT,
) -> ManagedProcess:
    """Start *argv* through *prefix* (which enters namespace *netns*) and return its handle.

    Returns only after the kernel has confirmed the requested *identity* for the
    process; raises :class:`ProcessStartError` (or :class:`IdentityError`) and
    leaves nothing running otherwise. stdin is ``/dev/null``. *stdout* and
    *stderr* are ``"capture"`` (at most *max_output_bytes* kept, the rest
    counted), ``"discard"``, or a path to a new file (mode 0600, never overwritten).
    """
    args = validate_argv(argv)
    requested = identity or ProcessIdentity()
    _check_kernel_supports(requested)
    if max_output_bytes < 0:
        raise ValueError("max_output_bytes must be non-negative")
    launcher = [resolve("setpriv"), *_setpriv_args(requested), "--"] if requested.requested else []

    fds: list[int] = []  # every descriptor opened here, closed on any failure
    handshake, chain_end = socket.socketpair()
    try:
        handshake.setblocking(False)
        out_fd, out_path, out_read = _open_output(stdout, fds)
        err_fd, err_path, err_read = _open_output(stderr, fds)
        command = [*prefix, *launcher, resolve("sh"), "-c", _PROBE, _LAUNCHER, *args]
        proc = await asyncio.create_subprocess_exec(
            *command,
            stdin=chain_end.fileno(),
            stdout=asyncio.subprocess.DEVNULL if out_fd is None else out_fd,
            stderr=asyncio.subprocess.DEVNULL if err_fd is None else err_fd,
            start_new_session=True,
            env=None if env is None else dict(env),
            cwd=cwd,
        )
    except BaseException:
        handshake.close()
        chain_end.close()
        for fd in fds:
            with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
                os.close(fd)
        raise

    # The child holds its ends now; the parent keeps the handshake and read ends.
    chain_end.close()
    for child_end in (out_fd, err_fd):
        if child_end is not None:
            os.close(child_end)
    pidfd = _pidfd(proc.pid)
    captures: dict[Stream, _Capture] = {}
    if out_read >= 0:
        captures["stdout"] = _Capture(out_read, max_output_bytes)
    if err_read >= 0:
        captures["stderr"] = _Capture(err_read, max_output_bytes)

    async def abandon() -> bytes:
        """Stop whatever the chain started; return what it wrote to stderr."""
        handshake.close()  # a waiting probe reads EOF and exits without exec
        try:
            await asyncio.wait_for(asyncio.shield(proc.wait()), 1.0)
        except asyncio.TimeoutError:
            if pidfd is not None:
                with contextlib.suppress(ProcessLookupError):
                    pidfd_send_signal(pidfd, signal.SIGKILL)
            await run_blocking(signal_namespace, netns, signal.SIGKILL, pgid=proc.pid)
            await proc.wait()
        stderr_capture = captures.get("stderr")
        if stderr_capture is not None:
            await stderr_capture.wait_eof(_OUTPUT_DRAIN)
        text = b"" if stderr_capture is None else bytes(stderr_capture.data)
        for capture in captures.values():
            capture.close()
        if pidfd is not None:
            os.close(pidfd)
        return text

    try:
        report = await asyncio.wait_for(_read_report(handshake), start_timeout)
    except asyncio.TimeoutError:
        stderr_text = await abandon()
        raise ProcessStartError(
            f"{args[0]!r} did not reach the identity check within {start_timeout}s",
            "timeout",
            stderr_text,
        ) from None
    except BaseException:
        await asyncio.shield(abandon())
        raise

    if report == _MISSING:
        stderr_text = await abandon()
        raise ProcessStartError(f"program {args[0]!r} not found", "program_not_found", stderr_text)
    observed: EffectiveIdentity | None = None
    if report.endswith(_REPORT_END):
        with contextlib.suppress(ValueError):
            observed = EffectiveIdentity.from_status(
                report[: -len(_REPORT_END)].decode(errors="replace")
            )
    if observed is None:
        stderr_text = await abandon()
        detail = stderr_text.decode(errors="replace").strip()
        raise ProcessStartError(
            f"the launch chain for {args[0]!r} failed before the identity check"
            + (f": {detail}" if detail else ""),
            "launch_failed",
            stderr_text,
        )
    problems = observed.mismatches(requested)
    if problems:
        await abandon()
        raise IdentityError(
            f"refusing to start {args[0]!r}: " + "; ".join(problems), observed, problems
        )

    started_at = time.time()
    try:
        await asyncio.get_running_loop().sock_sendall(handshake, b"go\n")
    finally:
        handshake.close()
    logger.info("Started %s (pid %d) as uid %d", args, proc.pid, observed.uids[1])
    return ManagedProcess(
        proc=proc,
        pidfd=pidfd,
        argv=args,
        command=command,
        netns=netns,
        identity=observed,
        started_at=started_at,
        captures=captures,
        paths=_paths(out_path, err_path),
    )
